title: 84% of New York's Sewer Backups Come From This #shorts
summary: Grease and debris caused 84% of New York City's sewer backups (NYC DEP, 2019); the city spends nearly $19 million a year on clogged sewers and wipes. Metro Vancouver spends over $2 million a year on wipes.
sources: Accumulation of grease and debris causes 84 percent of sewer backups in New York City; DEP spends nearly $19 million annually to clean clogged sewers, dispose of wipes and repair damaged machinery (NYC DEP press release, 21 Feb 2019): https://www.nyc.gov/html/dep/html/press_releases/19-008pr.shtml

Every year Metro Vancouver and its members spend over $2 million dealing with wipes and other unflushables, which can bind with other materials to clog sewers; pee, poo and toilet paper are the only things that are safe to flush (Metro Vancouver, Wipes): https://metrovancouver.org/wipes

scenes.narration: {84%|Eighty-four percent} of New York's sewer backups were caused by grease and debris.
Wipes don't help. They bind with other stuff and clog sewers.
New York spends nearly {$19 million|nineteen million dollars} a year on clogs and wipes.
Metro Vancouver spends over {$2 million|two million dollars} a year on wipes alone.
Its rule: pee, poo, toilet paper. Anything else can end up in that {84%|eighty-four percent}.
